title: Polynomial Functions: Zeros, Multiplicity, and End Behavior
seo_title: Polynomial Functions Worksheet: Zeros, Multiplicity, End Behavior (Algebra 2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 2 worksheet on polynomial functions: end behavior, zeros and multiplicity, writing polynomials from zeros, graphs and the Rational Root Theorem. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: End behavior comes from the leading term. Each factor (x − a) gives a zero at a.
key_sub: Even multiplicity touches the x-axis; odd multiplicity crosses it.
body_html:
How it works

End behavior depends only on the leading term. Even degree: both ends point the same way (up if the leading coefficient is positive). Odd degree: the ends point opposite ways (up on the right if the leading coefficient is positive).

In factored form, each factor (x − a) gives a zero at x = a. If the factor is squared (even multiplicity), the graph touches the axis and turns; with odd multiplicity it crosses.

A polynomial of degree n has exactly n complex zeros (counting multiplicity) and at most n − 1 turning points. Complex zeros of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs. The Rational Root Theorem lists the possible rational zeros: ± factors of the constant ÷ factors of the leading coefficient.

Example

Find the zeros of f(x) = (x + 2)(x − 3)².

x + 2 = 0 → −2 (crosses)

x − 3 = 0 → 3 (touches)

Answer: −2 and 3

Example

Write the polynomial with zeros 1, 2 and −3.

(x − 1)(x − 2)(x + 3)

Answer: x³ − 7x + 6

Common mistakes

  • Reading the zero of (x + 3) as 3. It is −3.
  • Judging end behavior from the constant or the first term written. Use the term with the highest power.
  • Ignoring multiplicity: a squared factor touches the axis instead of crossing it.
  • Forgetting that 2 + i comes with 2 − i.

faq.q: How do you find the end behavior of a polynomial?
faq.a: Look at the degree and the sign of the leading coefficient. Even degree: both ends the same direction. Odd degree: opposite directions.
How many times a factor appears. An even multiplicity means the graph touches the x-axis and turns around; an odd multiplicity means it crosses.

faq.q: What is the Rational Root Theorem?
faq.a: Any rational zero p/q of a polynomial with integer coefficients has p dividing the constant term and q dividing the leading coefficient.

faq.q: How many zeros does a polynomial have?
faq.a: A polynomial of degree n has exactly n complex zeros when you count multiplicity (the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

sets.title: Write a polynomial from its zeros

items.q: A cubic with real coefficients and leading coefficient 1 has zeros −3 and −2 + i. Write the polynomial.
items.e: Complex zeros come in conjugate pairs, so −2 − i is also a zero. Those two give x² + 4x + 5. Multiply by (x + 3): x³ + 7x² + 17x + 15.

items.q: Write the polynomial of least degree with leading coefficient 1 and zeros −5, 1, 4.
items.e: Each zero a gives a factor (x − a): (x + 5)(x − 1)(x − 4). Multiply out: x³ − 21x + 20.

items.q: A cubic with real coefficients and leading coefficient 1 has zeros −3 and −2 + 3i. Write the polynomial.
